catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Structural and domain architectural pattern catalogue derived from cas_runner source and cas-knowledge layout, excluding agentic prompt/LLM-loop patterns.
analysis_limits: Dynamic execution traces were not observed; structural analysis is inferred from static definitions, manifests, and file layouts.
Persistence mechanisms are file-system based (YAML, JSON, Markdown) rather than traditional relational/NoSQL databases.

system_map.overview: The CAS (Continuous Architecture System) runner provides an enterprise architecture governance pipeline. Structurally, it separates runtime coordination from disk-backed governance knowledge, relying on strongly typed domain models, deterministic health evaluations, transition registry machines, and workspace bootstrapping routines.

layers.name: Presentation & CLI Layer
layers.purpose: Provides user entry points, command dispatching, and environment argument parsing.

layers.name: Application Service & Orchestration Layer
layers.purpose: Coordinates governance workflows, state transition execution, and compliance engine runs.

layers.name: Domain Model Layer
layers.purpose: Defines core architectural entities, metrics, compliance findings, and capability sets using Pydantic.

layers.name: Infrastructure & IO Adapter Layer
layers.purpose: Handles external client communication, workspace initialization, filesystem artifact merging, and telemetry.

layers.name: Knowledge & Artifact Repository Layer
layers.purpose: Stores governance decisions, rules, patterns, evaluations, and steering projections as versioned disk artifacts.

components.role: Top-level pipeline execution controller coordinating execution flows.

components.name: GovernanceActionService
components.role: Application service encapsulating governance workflow operations.

components.name: GovernanceActionEngine & TransitionRegistry

orchestration.details: Executes sequential governance actions driven by the TransitionRegistry and compliance checks, reading file-based contexts and outputting structured reports.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity and Value Object Modeling
patterns.summary: Core governance and steering domains are modeled as explicit, strongly typed Pydantic models with built-in validation and serialization.
patterns.intent: Ensure architectural artifacts, metrics, and compliance findings conform to strict schemas across disk reads and service calls.
patterns.context: Architectural governance consumes unstructured or semi-structured data (markdown frontmatter, runtime evaluation JSONs, git diffs) that must be rigorously validated before ingestion.
forces: Need for schema evolution without breaking dynamic JSON deserialization.
Desire to catch malformed governance records early at the boundary.
Preserving immutability or strict typing across internal boundaries.
patterns.solution: Define domain models using Pydantic BaseModel with explicit typing, enums, and nested collections. Entities like GovernanceInventory, ComplianceMetrics, and CapabilityRecord express domain invariants directly.
implementation_signals: Use of Enum classes for categorical domain fields (e.g. GitChangeType, CapabilityCategory).
Explicit metric containers encapsulating health, throughput, and risk indicators.

evidence.note: Defines domain entities and metrics for governance compliance and operational tracking.
Defines steering projection entities, delta tracking models, and capability sets.

benefits: Self-documenting domain schemas with IDE type hinting.
Clear boundary separation between schema definitions and business logic.
costs: Runtime validation overhead during high-volume object instantiation.
Schema changes require coordinate updates across consumer components.
failure_modes: Validation errors raised unexpectedly if persisted JSON artifacts drift out of sync with updated model schemas.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standardize all domain modeling on Pydantic BaseModels and maintain shared types in designated `models.py` modules.

patterns.name: Declarative Transition Registry and Action Engine
patterns.summary: Encapsulates valid lifecycle transitions and actionable governance tasks within a centralized Transition Registry and execution engine.
patterns.intent: Prevent invalid status transitions of governance entities and provide a single dispatch point for lifecycle actions.
patterns.context: Architectural artifacts (e.g., decisions, patterns, rules) progress through statuses (e.g., proposed, accepted, deprecated). Actions must ensure transitions adhere to enterprise governance constraints.
forces: Ad-hoc state modifications across disparate modules lead to corrupted lifecycle states.
Need for auditing transition outcomes and providing traceable metrics.
patterns.solution: Centralize allowable state transitions inside TransitionRegistry, and execute validated state modifications via GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: Explicit registry class or mapping managing lifecycle source and target states.
Engine invoking registry validation prior to executing underlying domain changes.

evidence.note: Houses the registry defining state transitions and the engine that executes verified governance actions.

benefits: Enforces deterministic state transitions according to governance rules.
Decouples transition policy definitions from calling presentation or runner layers.
costs: Adding a new entity state requires updating registry definitions and handler methods.
failure_modes: Unregistered transitions cause action rejections, blocking downstream pipelines if transitions are incompletely specified.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use for any workflow where entities possess strict promotion or retirement lifecycles.

patterns.name: Pluggable Service Adapter Pattern
patterns.summary: Decouples external client dependencies through interchangeable production and test/mock client implementations.
patterns.intent: Isolate external remote services behind an adapter interface to enable seamless offline execution and unit testing.
patterns.context: The system connects to external LLM providers via LiteLLM, but offline execution, CI builds, and deterministic unit tests require hermetic mocking.
forces: Need to test governance logic without incurring external network calls or cloud costs.
Preserving a consistent client calling signature across runtime and test environments.
patterns.solution: Implement concrete client adapters alongside mock implementations (`LiteLLMClient` and `MockLLMClient`) presenting a consistent invocation interface.
implementation_signals: Co-located mock and real client classes sharing common operational signatures.
Conditional instantiation based on runtime flags or configuration.

evidence.note: Mock client delivering canned or deterministic responses without external network access.

benefits: Enables offline and air-gapped test execution.
Isolates external library breaking changes to the adapter module.
costs: Mock client must be maintained in sync with any interface changes to the production client.
failure_modes: Behavioral drift between mock responses and real provider responses.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standardize all remote or I/O-intensive service clients with a matching mock client adapter.

patterns.name: File-Backed Knowledge Repository
patterns.summary: Architectural truth and governance states are persisted directly in a structured file-system repository using human-readable YAML, JSON, and Markdown artifacts.
patterns.intent: Leverage Git version control and human-readable text formats as the primary persistence layer for enterprise architecture knowledge.
patterns.context: Enterprise architecture requires transparency, version traceability, and collaboration via pull requests. Traditional database-backed catalogs disconnect architecture records from codebase versioning.
forces: Need for versioning, diffing, and peer-reviewing architectural changes.
Avoiding complex external database dependencies for local CLI executions.
patterns.solution: Organize knowledge assets into standardized directory trees (`global/`, `governance/`, `runtime/`, `projects/`) containing structured Markdown with frontmatter, YAML execution profiles, and JSON contexts.
implementation_signals: Directory structures partitioning global, project, and runtime knowledge.
Template directories defining standardized schemas for decisions, patterns, and signals.
Runtime artifacts output as flat files (e.g. `runtime/execution-profile.yaml`, `runtime/rule-context.json`).

evidence.note: File-system layout functioning as the repository of governance and runtime state.

benefits: Complete GitOps compatibility: decisions, rules, and evolutions are reviewable via PRs.
Zero external database infrastructure requirements for runner execution.
costs: No built-in ACID transactions across multiple files.
Concurrency constraints when multiple automated agents or runners update the repository simultaneously.
failure_modes: Corrupted or partially written files during abnormal process termination.
Merge conflicts during concurrent Git pushes.

patterns.reuse_notes: Structure artifact folders by scope (global vs project vs runtime) and enforce standard templates.

patterns.name: Workspace Bootstrap and Template Injection
patterns.summary: Scaffolds new project repositories by injecting foundational governance blocks, directory structures, and standard templates.
patterns.intent: Ensure new or target repositories instantly adhere to organizational governance layouts without manual copy-pasting.
patterns.context: CAS runner targets external or local project repositories that need to be enrolled in continuous architecture governance.
forces: Manual repository setup creates inconsistent folder naming and missing templates.
Target projects may already have existing governance configs that must be merged rather than overwritten.
patterns.solution: Provide automated bootstrapping functions (`init_workspace`, `bootstrap`, `merge_cas_governance_block`) that initialize directories and merge standard configuration blocks idempotently.
implementation_signals: Functions dedicated to filesystem layout creation and template merging.
Idempotent merge logic for configuration files.

evidence.note: Provides workspace scaffolding and governance block merging.

benefits: Safe, idempotent updates to existing project configurations.
costs: Bootstrap templates must be kept synchronized with engine version changes.
failure_modes: Accidental corruption of existing user configurations if merging logic encounters unexpected syntax.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use dedicated bootstrap modules to enroll target repositories into the continuous governance lifecycle.

patterns.name: Deterministic Health and Compliance Evaluation
patterns.summary: Calculates categorical health states and evaluates rule compliance using pure, deterministic evaluation functions.
patterns.intent: Decouple rule evaluation and health scoring from side-effectful I/O, ensuring consistent and reproducible architecture audits.
patterns.context: Dashboard reporting and CI gates need an unambiguous measure of whether an architecture repository is healthy, degraded, or failing.
forces: Subjective or non-deterministic compliance checks lead to flaky CI build failures.
Metrics calculation must be explainable with actionable diagnostic reasons.
patterns.solution: Define dedicated evaluators (`HealthStatus`, `calculate_health`, `get_health_reasons`, `ComplianceEngine`) that take structured input models and return immutable status enums and finding arrays.
implementation_signals: Explicit enum for HealthStatus (e.g. Healthy, Degraded, Unhealthy).
Pure evaluation functions mapping metrics to status and diagnostic message arrays.
Compliance engine inspecting inventory models against predefined rules.

evidence.note: Computes health status and diagnostic reasons from architectural metrics.
Executes compliance checks against governance artifacts.

benefits: High testability via unit tests without mocking disk or network.
Actionable diagnostics: every non-healthy state provides exact reasons.
costs: Threshold changes require software releases or external configuration loading.
failure_modes: Misconfigured threshold values causing systemic false-positive compliance rejections.

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement health and compliance scoring as pure functions accepting typed metric models and returning reasons alongside enums.

anti_patterns.name: Direct File-System Coupling without Repository Abstraction
symptoms: Domain engines directly parsing file paths, hardcoded relative paths, or YAML/JSON loaders rather than querying a repository interface.
Difficulty unit testing governance workflows without creating temporary mock directories on disk.
impact: High coupling to disk structure making migration to alternative persistence (e.g., remote Git API, object storage) laborious.
Slow test suites dependent on file system I/O.
suggested_remediation: Introduce an explicit KnowledgeRepository or StoragePort protocol defining methods like `load_decisions()`, `save_rule()`, and `get_runtime_context()`.
Implement a FilesystemKnowledgeRepository and an InMemoryKnowledgeRepository for tests.

anti_patterns.name: Uncoordinated Multi-File State Mutation
symptoms: Governance actions updating multiple JSON, YAML, and Markdown files in sequence without an atomic staging or transaction mechanism.
Half-updated workspace states when an exception occurs mid-run.
impact: Inconsistent repository state if a process terminates abruptly or fails mid-step during continuous architecture updates.
suggested_remediation: Use a Unit of Work pattern or Git transaction staging area to verify all artifact updates succeed before committing or writing them to disk.
Ensure rollbacks revert uncommitted workspace modifications upon error.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Schema Serialization and Validation
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Utilizes Pydantic and JSONSchema to ensure contracts between disk-persisted metadata and in-memory domain structures remain strictly valid.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Distributed Tracing and Observability
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Instrumentation via OpenTelemetry (opentelemetry-api, opentelemetry-sdk) to observe governance runs and track execution traces across workflows.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Code Quality and Standards Enforcement
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Integrated static analysis and linting (Ruff, pyupgrade, flake8 bugbear) enforced with strict 88-char limits and Python 3.11/3.13 targets.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent modifications to `cas-knowledge` handled when multiple agents or CI jobs execute in parallel?
open_questions.context: The file-backed knowledge repository currently lacks explicit file locking or conflict resolution logic outside standard Git merges.

open_questions.question: Is there a formal Repository abstraction planned to insulate `ComplianceEngine` and `GovernanceActionEngine` from raw disk reads?
open_questions.context: Currently, engine modules directly traverse workspace paths and load files, which could complicate web-based or API-driven portal deployments.
